 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Akash Rathi - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Virendra Khadav -Govt. Adv. appearing on behalf of A  General.
 ORDER 1] They are heard and perused the case diary.

2] This is the applicant's third bail application filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 439 of Cr.P.C. as he/she is implicated in connection with Crime No.629/2022, registered at Police Station Raipuriya, District- Jhabua (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376(2)(n), 376(3) of the IPC & 5L/6 of the POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 13.04.2023.
Applicant's earlier bail applications have already been dismissed on merits.
3] The allegation against the applicant is of rape.

4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is lodged in jail since 13.4.2023; whereas the prosecutrix has also been examined in the trial on 03.2.2024 and although the prosecutrix has already been examined when the applicant's second bail application was rejected.

It is further submitted that admittedly, the prosecutrix has resided with the applicant for around five months NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24904 2 MCRC-35080-2025 as the date of the incident is 28.11.2022, and the prosecutrix has been recovered on 13.4.2023.
It is also submitted that the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take a long time.
Thus, it is prayed that the application be allowed.

sentences.text: 5] Counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the DNA is positive.

6] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case-diary, and taking note of the period of incarceration and the fact that the prosecutrix who had resided with the applicant for around five months and has also been examined in the trial court, this Court is inclined to allow the present application.
7] Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is hereby allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-
(rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

8] Accordingly, the application is allowed and disposed of .
C.c. as per rules.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE moni Shyam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2006917/
